supported_signed_accumulator: 40 x 64-bit limbs (2560-bit two's-complement); test includes signed endpoint -2^2559 and positive endpoint 2^2559-1

boundary_groups: zero and signed minimum subnormal units
positive and negative overflow midpoint around maximum finite binary64

oracles.name: python_integer_rounding_oracle
oracles.method: arbitrary-precision integer quotient/remainder with guard-equivalent half comparison and ties-to-even

oracles.name: python_decimal_rational_oracle
oracles.method: Decimal(units) / Decimal(2**1074), followed by CPython binary64 conversion

acceptance: The two Python oracles must agree bit-for-bit for every input; native C output bits must match the Decimal oracle for every input.
limitations: The Decimal oracle is not MPFR or SoftFloat and is not an independently verified numerical library.
Both Python oracles execute in the same Python runtime on each hosted runner.
The values are deterministic synthetic exact-unit sums, not representative scientific application workloads.
Hosted x86-64 and ARM64 runners are architecture-level CI replication, not independently provisioned physical hardware.
The C accumulator overflow precondition remains unchanged.
